title: Choose the visual world for Finances
question: The roll assigned Dutch rail signage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Station Signage
options.lineage: Dutch railway wayfinding and departure boards, Total Design lineage
options.thesis: Your money read like a departure board: what leaves before payday, and what is still yours.
options.viewport: Yellow top band with Overview / Money / Plan; free-to-spend as a big blue figure on white; a route strip from payday to payday with bills as stops and today as your position; 'Still to pay' set as a departure list.
options.risk: Yellow and blue are close to a real rail brand; it must stay signage discipline, never train costume.

raised.raise: Over plan is drawn as a hatch, not by red alone, so it reads in both themes and for colour-blind eyes.
One face on a strict size ladder; hierarchy comes from size steps, never from extra fonts.
Every category keeps fixed furniture (name, plan, left, next date) in the same spot wherever it appears.

options.label: Guilder Notes
options.thesis: Each kind of money gets its own note colour, and free-to-spend is printed like a denomination.
options.viewport: Free-to-spend as a huge expanded numeral in a sunflower-yellow field with fine line work; needs, wants and savings as three note-coloured bars; 'Needs you' and 'Still to pay' on white below.
options.risk: The most literal money reading; guilloche must stay a texture behind one number or it turns into decoration.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: The month as a friendly map: each kind of money is a flat colour area you can find your way around.
options.viewport: A big green area holding free-to-spend; capsule chips for what needs you; needs, wants and savings as three coloured areas with their bars inside.
options.case: Holds audience: warm and easy for the non-technical one of you. Loses on clarity: lobe shapes fight dense lists like Money.
options.risk: Can read as a toy for something as serious as money; the shapes cost layout effort on every page.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Load drawn as hatch density over a strict tonal ramp.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets per category, hatch for load.
options.case: Neither of you lives in a darkroom; the sheets hide the one number.
options.risk: Reads as a photographer's tool, not a household's.
options.kept: Conflict rendered without colour: over plan becomes a hatch.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A pixel-built figure over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both: no link to a Dutch household, and pixel figures slow reading money.
options.kept: One face at a strict size ladder.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Each category as a mascot with its own name plate.
options.viewport: A ranked grid of category mascots.
options.case: Loses both: cute, but 21 mascots bury what is over plan.
options.kept: Fixed personal furniture per item: same fields, same place.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One plant through the seasons at a fixed scale.
options.case: Loses both, and lands right back on cream plus italic serif.
options.risk: Exactly the AI look being left behind.
options.kept: Same scale across months, so months compare by eye (used on Money's trends).

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Categories as stars sized by spend.
options.case: Loses both: poetic, but nobody can read 'free until payday' off a sky.
options.kept: One fixed size ramp carries importance.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean budgeting app like Copilot or Monarch, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Free-to-spend card with pace chart, a review card, upcoming bills, budget bars; bottom tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other finance app by design.
